{
  "success_memory_items": [
    {
      "title": "Write a temporary self-test harness before trusting the implementation",
      "pattern": "After implementing the target module, immediately create a throwaway test script (e.g. selftest.mjs / tmp_selftest.mjs) that imports the real module and asserts expected outputs, then run it with node. Keep the harness separate from the deliverable and delete it before finishing.",
      "why_it_helps": "The hidden grader cannot be inspected, so a local harness is the only feedback loop. It converts the spec into executable checks, surfaces wrong assumptions early, and lets the agent iterate on the real module rather than guessing.",
      "examples": [
        "Wrote selftest.mjs importing { encode, decode } and asserting known ciphertexts, then ran `node selftest.mjs`.",
        "Wrote tmp_selftest.mjs for robot-name asserting name format, uniqueness across 300+ robots, and reset behavior.",
        "Wrote selfcheck.mjs for zebra-puzzle asserting waterDrinker()/zebraOwner() and that exactly one arrangement satisfies all facts."
      ],
      "scope": "Single-file JS exercises where the official test file is hidden.",
      "confidence": 0.95
    },
    {
      "title": "Use an independent reference implementation for differential testing",
      "pattern": "When the spec is algorithmic (ciphers, combinatorial enumeration, formatting), write a second, deliberately different implementation (brute force, exhaustive search, or direct formula) and compare its output against the primary implementation over many generated inputs.",
      "why_it_helps": "Two independent derivations of the same spec catch logic errors that a single implementation's own tests would share. It also validates edge cases the agent might not have thought to enumerate.",
      "examples": [
        "gen.mjs brute-forced the modular inverse over a in 1..25 and compared against the real encode/decode across many keys.",
        "verify2.tmp.mjs enumerated all reachable tic-tac-toe boards by legal play and compared against gamestate().",
        "killer-sudoku selftest included 'brute-force agreement (460 cases)' against a naive combination generator."
      ],
      "scope": "Exercises with well-defined mathematical or enumerable semantics.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Derive expected values from the problem statement, not from the implementation",
      "pattern": "Build the self-test's expected values by transcribing the examples and rules from the prompt (or by computing them with an independent method), rather than by running the implementation and copying its output.",
      "why_it_helps": "Prevents the classic failure mode where the test simply mirrors the bug. When the harness fails, the failure is meaningful because the expectation came from the spec.",
      "examples": [
        "space-age selftest used the prompt's stated 31.69 Earth-years and the planet orbital periods to compute expected values.",
        "bottle-song selftest embedded the full song text verbatim from the instructions as the expected array.",
        "affine-cipher selftest used the prompt's example ciphertexts (e.g. 'ybty' for encode('test',{a:5,b:7}))."
      ],
      "scope": "Any exercise where the prompt contains examples or explicit formulas.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Enumerate boundary and degenerate cases explicitly in the harness",
      "pattern": "Systematically include tests for: empty input, zero/negative values, out-of-range values, invalid keys, single-element ranges, and inputs that should throw. Assert both the value and the error behavior.",
      "why_it_helps": "Hidden graders typically weight edge cases heavily. Explicitly testing them forces the implementation to handle them rather than only the happy path.",
      "examples": [
        "triangle selftest covered 0,0,0 and degenerate 1,1,2 / 1,2,3 to pin down the >= inequality semantics.",
        "phone-number selftest asserted throws for exchange codes starting with 0 or 1 and for wrong length.",
        "affine-cipher selftest asserted that non-coprime a throws and that digits pass through unencrypted."
      ],
      "scope": "All exercises; especially those with validation rules.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Inspect the project scaffolding before writing code",
      "pattern": "Read package.json, babel.config.js, and the stub file first to learn the module system (ESM vs CJS), export names, and any build/transform setup, then match the implementation to that contract.",
      "why_it_helps": "Avoids import/export mismatches and syntax that the grader's toolchain rejects. It also reveals whether the stub throws and what the expected export shape is.",
      "examples": [
        "Read package.json and babel.config.js in nearly every run before writing the module.",
        "tournament run copied the module to a .mjs.js file to satisfy ESM import in the local harness after checking package.json.",
        "robot-name run attempted to read .exercism/config.json to confirm the exercise contract."
      ],
      "scope": "Any repo-based coding task with existing scaffolding.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Iterate: run harness, read failures, fix, re-run",
      "pattern": "Treat the self-test as a tight loop: run it, read the actual-vs-expected diff, adjust the implementation (or the harness if the expectation was wrong), and re-run until all cases pass.",
      "why_it_helps": "Converts debugging into a deterministic feedback cycle and prevents shipping code that was never executed. The traces show multiple runs converging from FAIL to ALL PASS.",
      "examples": [
        "affine-cipher: first run showed FAILs on 'Hello, World!' and 'Testing 1 2 3', then after fixes the harness reported ALL MATCH.",
        "parallel-letter-frequency: initial FAIL on punctuation and non-ASCII, then ALL PASS after correction.",
        "ocr-numbers: multiple iterations fixing glyph slicing until all cases passed."
      ],
      "scope": "All implementation tasks with a runnable harness.",
      "confidence": 0.9
    },
    {
      "title": "Clean up temporary artifacts and verify final syntax",
      "pattern": "Before finishing, delete all temporary test/reference files and run a syntax check (e.g. `node --check <file>`) plus a directory listing to confirm only the intended deliverable remains.",
      "why_it_helps": "Prevents stray files from confusing the grader or being mistaken for the solution, and confirms the final file parses. Several runs also grepped for leftover stub throws.",
      "examples": [
        "`rm -f selftest.mjs && node --check affine-cipher.js && ls -a`.",
        "`rm -f temp_diag.mjs temp_selftest.mjs && node --check bottle-song.js && grep -n 'Remove this statement' bottle-song.js || echo 'no stub throw left'`.",
        "`rm -f selfcheck.mjs && ls -la` after zebra-puzzle."
      ],
      "scope": "All single-file exercises.",
      "confidence": 0.85
    },
    {
      "title": "Reuse a known self-test skill/workflow when available",
      "pattern": "When a skill or memory describing the single-file JS self-test workflow exists, read it first and follow its structure (harness naming, assertion style, cleanup) instead of inventing a new approach each time.",
      "why_it_helps": "Standardizes the verification loop, reduces setup time, and encodes prior lessons about what the grader expects.",
      "examples": [
        "Nearly every run began with skill_read('stub-single-file-js-selftest').",
        "state-of-tic-tac-toe run also consulted memory_search/memory_read for expected return-value casing."
      ],
      "scope": "Environments that expose reusable skills or memory.",
      "confidence": 0.7
    }
  ]
}
